sections.content: If you've been searching for affordable real estate deals with strong upside potential, Akron, Ohio deserves a serious look. This mid-sized city in Northeast Ohio sits about 40 miles south of Cleveland and has quietly built a reputation among savvy investors for its low acquisition costs, improving neighborhoods, and steady rental demand. Whether you're brand new to the game — in which case our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide is a great place to start — or a seasoned wholesaler looking for your next market, Akron offers opportunities across multiple investment strategies.
Akron OH Real Estate Market Overview

Akron is Ohio's fifth-largest city with a population of around 190,000 people. Once known almost exclusively for rubber manufacturing, the city has been reinventing itself through healthcare, education, and technology sectors. The University of Akron and Summa Health System are two of the largest employers, providing a stable base of renters and buyers. Home values remain well below the national average, making it one of the more accessible markets for investors working with limited capital. The median home price in Akron sits around $130,000 to $145,000, compared to the national median of over $400,000. That gap is exactly why experienced investors are paying attention. You can explore current listings and deal flow specifically for this market at [aiwholesail.com/markets/akron-oh](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/akron-oh).
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Akron

Not every zip code in Akron is created equal for investors. Understanding which neighborhoods align with your strategy — whether that's flipping, wholesaling, or buy-and-hold — can make or break your returns.
Highland Square and West Akron

Highland Square is one of the most desirable neighborhoods for house flippers. It features walkable streets, local restaurants, and a growing arts scene that attracts young professionals. Homes here often sell for $150,000 to $220,000 after renovation, and distressed properties can be acquired for $60,000 to $90,000, leaving solid room for a profitable flip when you account for rehab costs.
North Hill

North Hill has seen significant revitalization investment and is popular with the rental crowd. Its proximity to downtown and a diverse immigrant community has spurred new businesses and foot traffic. Buy-and-hold investors can find two- and three-bedroom homes priced between $50,000 and $85,000 that rent for $800 to $1,100 per month, offering cash-on-cash returns that can exceed 12% when purchased right.
Kenmore and Ellet

Kenmore is a working-class neighborhood ideal for wholesale deals and rentals. Motivated sellers are relatively easy to find here due to higher vacancy rates and older housing stock. Ellet, on the other hand, is a more stable blue-collar neighborhood in the southeast part of the city where rentals maintain consistent occupancy and values have been slowly appreciating.

items: Highland Square: Best for flips, strong ARV, walkable amenity base
North Hill: Strong rental demand, lower acquisition costs, revitalization momentum
Kenmore: High wholesale deal volume, motivated sellers, entry prices under $60K
Ellet: Stable rentals, moderate appreciation, family-oriented demographics
Downtown Akron: Emerging condo and mixed-use opportunities near new development

sections.content: Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Akron
Wholesale Deals

Akron is a wholesaler-friendly market. The volume of distressed, vacant, and inherited properties keeps deal flow consistent throughout the year. Assignment fees typically range from $5,000 to $15,000 per deal, and because buyer pools are active, contracts move relatively quickly. If you're new to wholesaling, brush up on the fundamentals with our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide before jumping in. The key is finding motivated sellers before they hit the MLS — probate leads, tax-delinquent lists, and absentee owner data are your best sources.
Fix and Flip

Akron's fix-and-flip market rewards investors who do their homework on after-repair value (ARV). With median rehab costs running $25,000 to $55,000 depending on the scope of work, a successful flip can net $30,000 to $60,000 in profit on a well-sourced deal. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly estimate your post-renovation value before making an offer. Neighborhoods like Highland Square and Merriman Hills offer the strongest resale prices, while areas like Kenmore require tighter margins and more conservative ARV projections.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

The rental market in Akron is strong and getting stronger. Vacancy rates in desirable neighborhoods hover around 5% to 7%, and rent prices have increased roughly 8% to 12% over the past two years. Single-family homes in North Hill and Kenmore can generate gross monthly rents of $850 to $1,100, and small multifamily properties — two- to four-unit buildings — are particularly attractive for investors who want to maximize income per acquisition. With purchase prices still under $100,000 in many areas, achieving the 1% rule (monthly rent equals at least 1% of purchase price) is genuinely achievable in Akron.

Pro Tip: Before making any offer in Akron, run your numbers through our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to quickly determine your maximum allowable offer (MAO). In a market with thin margins like Kenmore, even a $5,000 miscalculation can turn a good deal into a break-even or loss.
Akron Real Estate Market Trends to Watch

Several trends are shaping the Akron investment landscape heading into 2024 and beyond. First, remote work migration from higher-cost metros like Cleveland and Columbus is increasing housing demand in Akron's more affordable zip codes. Second, the city has committed over $100 million in redevelopment funding toward downtown infrastructure and mixed-use projects, which historically lifts surrounding residential values. Third, institutional investors have not yet saturated this market the way they have in Columbus or Cincinnati, meaning individual investors still have a competitive edge when sourcing off-market deals.

"The best real estate markets for individual investors aren't the ones everyone is already talking about — they're the ones quietly showing the fundamentals: job growth, population stability, and housing demand that outpaces supply." — Common wisdom among experienced Midwest real estate investors

One trend worth monitoring is property tax assessments. Summit County (where Akron is located) conducted reassessments recently that pushed values higher in some neighborhoods, which can affect cash flow projections for rental investors. Always factor in current tax bills — not old ones — when underwriting a deal.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Akron

The most profitable real estate deals in Akron OH rarely appear on Zillow or the MLS. Off-market sourcing is where serious investors build their edge. Direct mail campaigns targeting tax-delinquent or absentee owners, driving for dollars in transitional neighborhoods, and building relationships with local probate attorneys are all proven strategies. For a deeper dive into these methods, check out our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals). In Akron specifically, attending local REIA (Real Estate Investors Association) meetups is also valuable — the Northeast Ohio REIA has an active membership base that regularly shares deal flow and buyer lists.

items: Pull tax-delinquent lists from Summit County Fiscal Office
Target absentee owners in North Hill and Kenmore with direct mail
Connect with probate attorneys in the Akron area for estate sale leads
Use driving-for-dollars apps to identify vacant and distressed properties
Network at Northeast Ohio REIA meetings for buyer and seller referrals
Build relationships with local wholesalers who may have overflow deals

sections.content: Tips for Out-of-State Investors Eyeing Akron
Akron is genuinely investor-friendly for out-of-state buyers, but remote investing requires a reliable local team. Here's what you need to know before writing your first offer from out of town.

items: Build your team first: Find a local property manager, contractor, and real estate attorney before you close your first deal
Visit the market at least once: Drive the neighborhoods yourself — Google Street View doesn't show you everything about a block
Understand Summit County property taxes: They can run $1,500 to $3,500 annually on typical investment properties, which affects cash flow significantly
Use virtual tools wisely: Platforms and data tools can help you screen deals remotely before committing to deeper due diligence
Account for Ohio landlord-tenant law: Ohio is considered a relatively landlord-friendly state, but understand the eviction process timeline before you buy
Check flood zones: Some parts of Akron near the Cuyahoga River require flood insurance, which adds to your operating costs

sections.content: Learning [how to analyze real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) with precision is especially critical when you can't walk a property in person. Remote investors should be even more conservative with their ARV estimates and rehab budgets to create a larger margin of safety on every deal.

Pro Tip: When investing remotely in Akron, require your contractor to provide a detailed scope of work with line-item pricing before closing. Add a 15% to 20% contingency buffer on top of that estimate. Older housing stock in Summit County often reveals surprises — knob-and-tube wiring, cast iron plumbing, and foundation issues are common in homes built before 1950.
Is Akron the Right Market for You?

Real estate deals in Akron OH offer something increasingly rare in today's market: genuine affordability paired with real income potential. The city isn't without its challenges — some neighborhoods require patience and a long-term view, and absentee ownership has left pockets of blight that take time to turn around. But for investors willing to do their homework, build a local team, and underwrite deals conservatively, Akron consistently delivers strong cash-on-cash returns, flip profits, and wholesale assignment fees that are harder to find in pricier metros. The fundamentals are in place. The deal flow is real. The question is whether you're ready to move on it.
